Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual reduction for average earners. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector net debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support includes maintaining corporation tax rates, extending "full expensing" to leasing when conditions allow, and a ten-point plan for SMEs covering business rates relief, VAT threshold reviews, and improved access to finance.

## Taxation and Pensions

The "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure State Pensions rise annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, while introducing a new age-related personal allowance to prevent pensioners being drawn into income tax. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household-based system, with withdrawal beginning at £120,000 combined income.

## Immigration

Proposals include a legally binding annual cap on migration covering work and family visas, with Parliament voting on levels each year. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue, alongside reforms to asylum rules and increased visa fees. Health checks for migrants would be introduced, with potential Immigration Health Surcharge increases.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. Plans include continued Ukraine support, nuclear deterrent modernisation, and a National Defence and Resilience Plan.

## Healthcare

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. Pharmacy First expansion, 250 new or modernised GP surgeries, and 50 Community Diagnostic Centres are planned. Social care cost caps would be implemented from October 2025.

## Housing

The target is 1.6 million new homes, achieved through brownfield development fast-tracking, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Education and Skills

Proposals include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, and the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education. Mobile phones would be banned during school hours.

## Energy and Environment

Annual oil and gas licensing rounds would continue, alongside trebling offshore wind capacity and building Small Modular Reactors. Green levies on household bills would be kept lower than 2023 levels. Net zero by 2050 remains the target.

## Transport

£36 billion from HS2 savings would fund regional transport improvements, including £8.3 billion for road maintenance. The £2 bus fare cap would continue throughout the Parliament. Measures would prevent road pricing and reverse London's ULEZ expansion.

## Welfare Reform

Plans include reforming disability benefits assessment, tightening work capability assessments, and introducing stricter sanctions for those refusing suitable employment after 12 months. Projected savings total £12 billion annually.
